es: Escribir una crítica matizada de una publicación: dos críticas justificadas, una relación con modal de duda y una alternativa razonable.

vocabulary.es: no alcanzar, quedarse corto respecto a

teaching.en: The post seems to overlook the size of the sample, which is arguably its most serious weakness.
teaching.es: La publicación parece pasar por alto el tamaño de la muestra, que es posiblemente su debilidad más seria.
teaching.explanationEs: Seems to + verbo base suaviza la crítica; arguably la hace discutible en lugar de tajante.
segments: The post seems to overlook the size of the
sample, which is arguably its most serious weakness.
teaching.audioText: The post seems to overlook the size of the sample, which is arguably its most serious weakness.

teaching.en: The link between the two charts is tenuous, so the evidence may fall short of what such a bold claim requires.
teaching.es: El vínculo entre los dos gráficos es tenue, así que la evidencia puede quedarse corta para una afirmación tan audaz.
teaching.explanationEs: Fall short of + sustantivo: no llegar al nivel exigido.
segments: The link between the two charts is tenuous, so the evidence
may fall short of what such a bold claim requires.
teaching.audioText: The link between the two charts is tenuous, so the evidence may fall short of what such a bold claim requires.

teaching.en: Whether the survey was fair is open to question, because its method has never been put through public scrutiny.
teaching.es: Que la encuesta fuera justa es discutible, porque su método nunca se ha sometido a un examen público.
teaching.explanationEs: Open to question lleva to, no for; scrutiny es incontable.
segments: Whether the survey was fair is open to question, because
its method has never been put through public scrutiny.
teaching.audioText: Whether the survey was fair is open to question, because its method has never been put through public scrutiny.

teaching.en: To some extent the complaint is fair, but it is arguably a symptom of the new rules rather than a cause of anything.
teaching.es: Hasta cierto punto la queja es justa, pero posiblemente sea un síntoma de las nuevas normas y no la causa de nada.
teaching.explanationEs: Rather than + sustantivo contrapone dos ideas y deja clara la preferida.
segments: To some extent the complaint is fair, but it is arguably a
symptom of the new rules rather than a cause of anything.
teaching.audioText: To some extent the complaint is fair, but it is arguably a symptom of the new rules rather than a cause of anything.

teaching.en: A balanced critique puts a post under scrutiny, can raise doubts about one weak step and still propose a reasonable alternative.
teaching.es: Una crítica equilibrada somete la publicación a examen, puede generar dudas sobre un paso débil y aun así proponer una alternativa razonable.
teaching.explanationEs: La crítica matizada duda de un punto, no rechaza todo el texto.
segments: A balanced critique puts a post under scrutiny, can raise doubts
about one weak step and still propose a reasonable alternative.
teaching.audioText: A balanced critique puts a post under scrutiny, can raise doubts about one weak step and still propose a reasonable alternative.

teaching.en: The rise in complaints is likely to be linked to the new rules, but a tenuous link calls for cautious verbs.
teaching.es: Es probable que el aumento de quejas esté relacionado con las nuevas normas, pero un vínculo tenue pide verbos cautelosos.
teaching.explanationEs: Is likely to be + participio expresa probabilidad sin afirmar una causa.
segments: The rise in complaints is likely to be linked to the
new rules, but a tenuous link calls for cautious verbs.
teaching.audioText: The rise in complaints is likely to be linked to the new rules, but a tenuous link calls for cautious verbs.

prompt.es: ¿Qué versión formula mejor una crítica con matices?

choices.text: The post is nonsense, because nobody should trust any writer who loves bans so much.
The post is completely right, although it might still need one more good example.
The post seems to overlook other changes, so the ban may explain only part of it.

feedback.es: La primera crítica es cauta y razonada: señala un punto que se pasa por alto y deja abierta la explicación.

hint.es: Busca la crítica que da una razón concreta y usa un verbo de cautela.

origin.text: Since the school banned sweets, pupils have become calmer. The ban obviously works, and every school should copy it at once.

prompt.es: Completa: «Sus resultados no alcanzan lo que exige una afirmación general.»

feedback.es: Fall short of describe lo que no llega al nivel exigido; aquí, dos clases de veinte no bastan para generalizar.

hint.es: Verbo de la colocación ___ short of.

origin.text: The writer surveyed only two classes out of twenty. Her findings ___ short of what a general claim requires.

prompt.es: Ordena: «En lugar de culpar a los alumnos, pregunta por qué están cansados.»

answer.text: Rather than blaming students ask why they are tired
accepted: Rather than blaming students ask why they are tired
Ask why they are tired rather than blaming students

feedback.es: Rather than + gerundio contrapone una acción rechazada (culpar) con la preferida (preguntar).

hint.es: Empieza con Rather than y un gerundio; después va la orden.

prompt.es: ¿Qué sostiene la crítica sobre la relación entre ir en bici y las notas?

choices.text: That it is real but small, because only two classes were compared.
That it is pure coincidence, since only two classes were surveyed.
That it is reversed, because good marks make pupils want to cycle.
That it is weak, because richer or fitter pupils may explain both.

feedback.es: La crítica llama «tenuous» a la relación porque alumnos con más recursos o mejor forma física podrían explicar ambos datos.

origin.text: The post claims that cycling to school improves marks. Arguably, its main weakness is the sample: only two classes, both in richer districts. The link between cycling and marks is tenuous, since fitter or better-off pupils may cycle more and also study better. A reasonable alternative would be to compare pupils from different districts.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige la actitud de la locutora hacia la publicación de su amiga.

choices.text: Friendly but firm: she questions the method and proposes a fairer test.
Friendly but evasive: she hides her doubts and lets the post stand.
Critical only: she lists the flaws and suggests no better test.
Sceptical of the app: she doubts that any app can be tested fairly.

feedback.es: Sus dudas son concretas (tres días, sin comparación) y propone una alternativa: una crítica amable pero firme.

origin.audio: My friend's post about a new app was kind, but I had two concerns. First, she had used it for only three days, so her praise may fall short of a fair test. Second, she compared it with nothing. I suggested that she try another app for a week and report both results. She laughed, then agreed that her post was open to question.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con la función que cumple en una crítica.

pairs: The post seems to overlook the sample.
To some extent the claim is fair.
A reasonable alternative would be to ask every class.
The rise is likely to be linked to the rules.

feedback.es: Cada frase cumple un papel distinto: crítica cautelosa, concesión, propuesta y relación probable.

pairs: The post seems to overlook the sample.
To some extent the claim is fair.
A reasonable alternative would be to ask every class.
The rise is likely to be linked to the rules.

prompt.es: ¿Qué crítica de la publicación resulta más sólida y equilibrada?

choices.text: It proves that silence works, although a few pupils disliked it at first.
Its evidence is a few interviews and anecdotes, so a national rule is open to question.
It relies on teachers' opinions alone, so the pupils' view is missing entirely.
It should have interviewed every single pupil, because three opinions can never mean anything.

feedback.es: La crítica válida señala el punto débil (pocas entrevistas y unas anécdotas) y duda de la generalización, sin rechazar toda la publicación.

origin.text: Last term our school introduced a silent lunch hour, and the results are surprising. Complaints about noise fell by half, and teachers say that afternoon lessons are calmer. One teacher told me that pupils now return to class ready to work. Some students complained at first, but they soon adapted. I interviewed three of them, and all three admitted that they prefer the quiet. A parent also told me that her son comes home less tired and does his homework without any argument. So the policy is a success, and every school in the country should adopt it immediately, because silence is exactly what teenagers need.

prompt.es: Completa: «El método de la encuesta puede generar dudas sobre la conclusión.»

feedback.es: Raise doubts about es la colocación habitual para una objeción razonable sobre un método o una conclusión.

origin.text: The numbers in the report are accurate. However, the survey method may ___ doubts about the conclusion, because nobody checked how the pupils were chosen.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige lo que la locutora deja entrever con el final de la historia.

choices.text: That the author was offended and chose to end the discussion.
That the critic had been rude in his last message to her.
That the author may have had no good answer to that point.
That the survey was repeated and confirmed the pattern.

feedback.es: El silencio final sugiere que la autora no tenía buena respuesta a la última objeción; el texto no dice que se ofendiera ni que repitiera la encuesta.

origin.audio: The author of the post replied politely. She accepted that her sample was small, but insisted that the pattern was clear. The critic answered that a clear pattern in a small sample is exactly what chance produces, and asked whether she would repeat the survey with more classes. The author did not reply again.

prompt.es: Escribe una crítica matizada de la publicación (220–280 palabras).

answer.text: The post makes an interesting point, but I think its conclusion needs more care. First, the writer seems to overlook the size of the sample: only thirty pupils from one class were asked, so the result may fall short of what a general claim requires. Second, the post rests on the idea that headphones stop fights, but it gives no evidence of how the fights were counted, which leaves the method open to question. To some extent, the fall in fights is likely to be linked to the headphones, although other factors, such as the weather or a new teacher, may also account for it. Arguably, the pupils who use headphones are simply the quiet ones, so the link is tenuous. Rather than handing out headphones in every school, a reasonable alternative would be to survey several classes for a whole term and compare the results. A balanced critique must also admit that the idea is worth testing, and I would certainly support a careful trial.
accepted: The post makes an interesting point, but I think its conclusion needs more care. First, the writer seems to overlook the size of the sample: only thirty pupils from one class were asked, so the result may fall short of what a general claim requires. Second, the post rests on the idea that headphones stop fights, but it gives no evidence of how the fights were counted, which leaves the method open to question. To some extent, the fall in fights is likely to be linked to the headphones, although other factors, such as the weather or a new teacher, may also account for it. Arguably, the pupils who use headphones are simply the quiet ones, so the link is tenuous. Rather than handing out headphones in every school, a reasonable alternative would be to survey several classes for a whole term and compare the results. A balanced critique must also admit that the idea is worth testing, and I would certainly support a careful trial.

I found the post interesting, but its argument needs more care. To begin with, the writer seems to overlook how small the sample was: thirty pupils from a single class cannot speak for a whole school, so the evidence falls short of a general rule. Besides, the post never explains how the fights were counted, and that raises doubts about the method. To some extent, the calmer breaks are likely to be linked to the headphones, but a new teacher, better weather or a different timetable could also account for them. Arguably, the link is tenuous, because quiet pupils may be the ones who choose headphones. Rather than giving headphones to every school, a reasonable alternative would be to compare several classes over a full term. A balanced critique should add that the idea deserves a serious trial, and I would gladly help to organise one, even if the final results turned out to be smaller than the post promises.

feedback.es: Una crítica matizada nombra dos debilidades con su razón, relaciona dos datos con duda, concede un punto y propone una alternativa.

origin.text: Publicación del blog del colegio: «Desde que los alumnos usan auriculares en el recreo hay menos peleas. Los auriculares evitan los conflictos y deberían repartirse en todos los colegios.» La encuesta incluyó solo a 30 alumnos de una clase. Escribe dos críticas justificadas, una relación con modal de duda y una alternativa razonable.

prompt.es: ¿Con qué intención escribe Luna su correo?

choices.text: To explain why the new bell makes the timetable a failure.
To praise the argument while asking Mar to correct a few small mistakes in her figures.
To reject the post as unreliable and ask Mar to delete it.
To voice constructive doubts and suggest a fairer comparison.

feedback.es: Luna elogia el argumento, señala dos puntos discutibles y propone comparar con otro colegio: una crítica constructiva.

origin.text: Dear Mar, thank you for sharing your post about the new timetable. I enjoyed the argument, but two points seem open to question. You say that lessons are shorter because pupils are happier, yet the change may simply be due to the new bell. Could you check the numbers again? A comparison with another school would be a reasonable alternative. Best wishes, Luna.

prompt.es: Completa: «En concreto, la conexión es tenue: los gráficos van por caminos distintos.»

feedback.es: Tenuous describe un vínculo débil; los once meses en que los gráficos divergen lo dejan casi sin apoyo.

origin.text: Both charts rose in January, which is why the post links them. On closer reading, the connection is ___: the charts go different ways for eleven other months.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Que la encuesta hable por todos es discutible.»

answer.text: Whether the survey speaks for everyone is open to question

feedback.es: Whether + oración funciona como sujeto, y open to question cierra el comentario con la colocación correcta.
